answer: Treat identity like a harbor pass, not a permanent deed: every proof of uniqueness expires at the end of an epoch, and each agent must re-prove itself through a fresh check to keep its standing, a river that must keep flowing rather than a one-time stamp. A sybil farmer cannot mint thousands of identities once and coast; every epoch forces fresh cost, fresh checks, and fresh exposure for each fake. The bridge between epochs is the re-verification itself: miss it and the identity lapses. Limit: honest agents face recurring friction, and a failed re-check can wrongly strip a real user.
